chunks: 9-14 Abu Muhammad al-Hasan ibn Hamzah al-'Alawi, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated to us. He said: Yusuf ibn Muhammad al-Tabari narrated to me, from Sahl Abi 'Umar, who said: Waki' narrated to us, from Zakariya ibn Abi Za'idah, from 'Amir al-Sha'bi, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام spoke nine sayings spontaneously. They outshone the sources of eloquence, singularized the jewels of wisdom, and prevented all people from attaining even one like them. Three of them are in intimate supplication, three in wisdom, and three in etiquette.
As for those in wisdom, he said: "The value of every person is what he does well. No person who knows his worth is ruined. A man is hidden beneath his tongue."

As for those in etiquette, he said: "Bestow favor upon whomever you wish, and you will be his master. Need whomever you wish, and you will be his captive. Be independent of whomever you wish, and you will be his equal."

As for those in intimate supplication, he said: "My God, it is enough honor for me that I be Your servant, and it is enough pride for me that You be my Lord. You are as I love, so make me as You love."

key_terms.أَسِيرَهُ: his captive; figuratively bound through dependence and need
key_terms.الْأَدَبِ: etiquette; refined conduct and proper human behavior
key_terms.الْحِكْمَةِ: wisdom; profound moral and intellectual insight
key_terms.الْمُنَاجَاةِ: intimate supplication; private devotional address to Allah
key_terms.عَبْدًا: servant; one devoted in worship and belonging to Allah
key_terms.قَدْرَهُ: his measure or proper worth; self-knowledge of one’s limits and station
key_terms.قِيمَةُ: value or worth; a person’s true measure
key_terms.مَخْبُوءٌ: hidden or concealed; not fully known until revealed

ai.seo_question: What are the nine celebrated sayings of Imam Ali عليه السلام on wisdom, etiquette, and supplication?
ai.summary: This hadith preserves nine concise sayings of Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام, divided into wisdom, etiquette, and intimate supplication. They emphasize self-knowledge, the measure of a person through speech and excellence, the dynamics of need and generosity in human relations, and the servant’s honor in devotion to Allah.
